sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Scrapling is a Python web scraping framework. It combines fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers for JavaScript pages, powerful parsing and concurrent crawling in one library, and can also be used from the terminal or by AI agents through an MCP server.
sixtySeconds.problem: Scraping modern sites usually means stitching together a request library, a headless browser, a parser and a crawler. Scrapling provides all of these with one API, plus retries, proxy rotation, pause and resume, and exports.
whoFor: AI agent builders who need web extraction through MCP
Researchers turning websites into clean Markdown
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want one Python library that goes from a single page to a full crawl. Only scrape sites you are allowed to, and respect their terms and robots rules.
requirements: Browser dependencies (installed by scrapling install) only if you need browser fetchers

overview: Scrapling can fetch pages with fast HTTP requests or stealth browsers that render JavaScript, keep persistent sessions and capture background API calls. Parsing supports CSS, XPath, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking that survives page changes, similar-element matching and clean Markdown output.

Spiders crawl concurrently with proxy rotation, retries, AutoThrottle, pause and resume, streaming and exports to JSON, JSONL, CSV and XML. You can use it from Python, from the terminal with an interactive shell, or from AI agents through its MCP server and Agent Skill.

The base pip install includes only the parser. Install the fetchers extra and run scrapling install to download browsers, or add ai, rag or shell extras for the MCP server, RAG helpers and the shell. Docker images are also published.

firstRun.title: Fetch a page and print quotes
firstRun.code:
from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher
page = Fetcher.get('https://quotes.toscrape.com/')
quotes = page.css('.quote .text::text').getall()
print(quotes)
